samples.summary: New copy-refusal guard (`documentHasTableAtNestingCap` → BadRequestException) has no test at all
samples.evidence: document-copy.service.ts:446 adds a user-visible 400 on the copy path ('Cannot copy this document…'). I grepped packages/backend for `documentHasTableAtNestingCap`, `nesting`, `nested`, `too deeply` — the only hits are in the source, docs-tree.spec.ts (which tests `writeDocsRoot`, not the copy path) and the controller specs. document-copy.service.spec.ts contains no reference to nesting. So neither the refusal (deep doc ⇒ 400, source untouched) nor the non-regression (ordinary doc still copies with this new check in the path) is exercised; a false positive here would break document copying entirely and a removed check would silently drop a peer's rows during copy.

finding.summary: New copy-refusal guard (`documentHasTableAtNestingCap` → BadRequestException) has no test at all
finding.evidence: document-copy.service.ts:446 adds a user-visible 400 on the copy path ('Cannot copy this document…'). I grepped packages/backend for `documentHasTableAtNestingCap`, `nesting`, `nested`, `too deeply` — the only hits are in the source, docs-tree.spec.ts (which tests `writeDocsRoot`, not the copy path) and the controller specs. document-copy.service.spec.ts contains no reference to nesting. So neither the refusal (deep doc ⇒ 400, source untouched) nor the non-regression (ordinary doc still copies with this new check in the path) is exercised; a false positive here would break document copying entirely and a removed check would silently drop a peer's rows during copy.

verdict.reason: The guard is real and untested. document-copy.service.ts:446-451 throws BadRequestException('Cannot copy this document: it contains a table nested too deeply...') on the 'doc' copy path via documentHasTableAtNestingCap (docs-tree.ts:250). I searched beyond the reviewer's queries: repo-wide for documentHasTableAtNestingCap/hasDocsTableAtNestingCap (only two call sites, no spec references), for the literal message strings (only docs-content validation/controller specs, which cover a different throw site in docs-content.controller.ts:454 for request bodies), for MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH in backend tests (only docs-tree.spec.ts:711-757, which asserts writeDocsRoot's own Error(/nested at or past/), not the copy service's 400), and for `tableData` anywhere under packages/backend (only docs-tree.* and docs-content.* — no copy spec or e2e spec ever constructs a nested table, so no test can reach the branch under another name). I also checked packages/backend/test/document-copy-attached.e2e-spec.ts, template.e2e-spec.ts and the CLI tests: none build a deep document for copy. One correction to the finding: the non-regression half IS partly covered — document-copy.service.spec.ts:219-262 copies a real doc root through real readDocsRoot/writeDocsRoot and therefore does traverse the new check — but that fixture has no table, so only the false branch is exercised; the refusal branch (deep doc => 400, row rolled back, source untouched) has no test at all. Major stands: a new user-visible 400 on the copy path can regress in either direction with nothing to catch it.

finding.summary: The render-path merge-expansion budget is only tested as a parameter, never through `computeSelectionRects` — dropping the argument at the call site would fail no test
finding.evidence: selection.ts:715 is the only place `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS` is passed. The new tests in packages/docs/test/view/cell-range-expand.test.ts call `expandCellRangeForMerges(..., 1000)` / `(..., 1<<18)` directly and `Selection.getNormalizedRange` (the unbudgeted path); grep for `computeSelectionRects` shows only selection-line-affinity.test.ts and image-selection-tint.test.ts use it, neither with a pathological table. So the wiring that actually protects the paint — the stated hazard ('one peer's presence hangs everyone's tab') — has no coverage: remove the budget argument and the suite stays green.

verdict.reason: The budget constant is wired in exactly one place — `normalizeRange(range, layout, MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS)` at selection.ts:715, reached only via `computeSelectionRects` (and `Selection.getSelectionRects`, selection.ts:908-916). No test exercises that wiring with input where the budget matters. The new tests in cell-range-expand.test.ts:210-276 pass budgets explicitly to `expandCellRangeForMerges` (1000, 4, 1<<18), i.e. they test the parameter, and the `Selection.getNormalizedRange` cases (lines 122-194, and the clamp case at nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:389-409) go through the deliberately unbudgeted path (selection.ts:905). The tests that do reach `computeSelectionRects` use non-table ranges (selection-line-affinity.test.ts:82, image-selection-tint.test.ts:162) or, indirectly through `editor.render()`, a 4x3 table with one ordinary merge (table-drag-merge-selection.test.ts) — all of which produce identical rectangles whether the budget is 2^18 or Infinity. I also searched every `*.test.ts` under packages/ for `budget`/`1 << 18`/`262144`, all test files mentioning `tableCellRange` in packages/docs and packages/frontend, and source-text-assertion style tests (readFileSync) in docs tests; none assert the call-site argument. So deleting the third argument at selection.ts:715 leaves the suite green, and the guard it removes is the one protecting the per-peer-per-paint expansion from a peer-chosen table size — a silently weakened DoS guard, hence major.
